about: The coverage each assembly reaches, held in both directions. A score under its entry is a suite that weakened; a score over its entry is an entry that has stopped describing the tree it sits in, and both are refused. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below and write the percentage the check prints for that assembly. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent, and since #188 a floor left under the measured score reds it too, so the sentence is now held rather than only written. Do not round the report's rate attribute down by hand. A rate is written to at most four decimal places and the attribute carries the float form of that value, so 0.9583 is stored as 0.9582999999999999, and rounding those digits down records a hundredth less than the suite reaches. That is where two of the four entries below sat until this file was corrected. The printed percentage is the same rate multiplied by a hundred and rounded to two decimals, which moves nothing while the report keeps to four, and the check compares the rate itself with a billionth of a point of slack for the float form, so a floor taken off the printed row compares equal rather than above. A collector that starts writing a fifth decimal would break that, and the repair then is to read the rate rather than the row.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.measured: line-rate 0.93 and branch-rate 1 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above run on Windows against the branch running a compiled query, with 937 tests passing on each leg. THE LINE FLOOR WENT DOWN AND THAT IS AN ADAPTER ARRIVING RATHER THAN THE SUITE WEAKENING. LibraryManagerItemSource is the server side of the port an evaluation asks its query through, five sequence points at hits=0, and it is unreachable by any test for the reason LibraryManagerChangeSource beside it is: the only way to execute it is to hold a real ILibraryManager, which means a running server. Nothing that was executed before this change stopped being executed, and no test was removed. The assembly went from 742 of 788 sequence points to 744 of 800: twelve sequence points arrive, two of them executed and ten not, and the ten are the adapter and the registration line beside it. Branch coverage is unmoved at 160 of 160, because the adapter declares no branch. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes. THE FIGURES THIS ENTRY CARRIED BEFORE were line-rate 0.9416 and branch-rate 1, taken against the branch landing the administrator API with 823 tests passing on each leg; that entry's account of which endpoints are reached is unchanged by this and is not restated here.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.lineNote: Three classes hold everything unexecuted in this assembly, and the third arrived with the evaluation port. Plugin.cs is at line-rate 0.0714 and needs a server to construct. LibraryManagerChangeSource is at line-rate 0: a constructor and six event accessors forwarding to the server's own library manager. LibraryManagerItemSource is at line-rate 0 for the same reason: a constructor and one forward onto ILibraryManager.GetItemList. What the suite covers instead is the type on the other side of each port, LibraryChangeSubscription and RuleEvaluator, both against a fake. PluginServiceRegistrator is at line-rate 1, RuleDocumentStore is at line-rate 1, and LibraryChangeCoalescer is at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: NO PARTIALLY COVERED BRANCH POINT IS LEFT IN THIS ASSEMBLY, which is what the branch figure of 1 says and is the one direction of this entry that cannot rise again. A branch added tomorrow that no test reaches reds this entry immediately rather than eroding a fraction. The evaluation adapter that lowered the line figure adds no branch point at all, which is why the two figures moved in different directions in one change. THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE described a six-clause name check in RuleDocumentStore as the only partial point and read: Every partially covered branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. That check is now a predicate the store and the API both ask, and both of its answers are reached from both callers, which is what closed it.

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.measured: line-rate 0.9994 and branch-rate 0.9984 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above run on Windows against the branch running a compiled query, with 937 tests passing on each leg. THE BRANCH FLOOR ROSE AND THE LINE FLOOR DID NOT. What raised it is the step that runs a compiled query and the post-query stage under it: the port, the reading of a field off an item, the comparison of a condition against one, the walk that decides which conditions may reach the query and the walk that judges an item against the composition tree. Every arm of all of them is reached, including the two that no document can produce and that are therefore reached with a fixture: a field the vocabulary does not declare, and a reading of a shape no reader produces. The assembly went from 3424 of 3426 sequence points and 994 of 996 branch slots to 3976 of 3978 and 1262 of 1264, so five hundred and fifty-two executed lines and two hundred and sixty-eight covered branch slots arrive and nothing unexecuted arrives with them. The line rate is unmoved for the truncation reason this entry has recorded before: 0.999416 and 0.999497 both truncate to 0.9994. THE ONE UNREACHED ARM IS STILL THE ONLY ONE and is the same discard it has always been. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.branchNote: The only partially covered branch point in the assembly is still the discard in the value-kind description in RuleDocumentValidator, reported at condition-coverage 87.5% (7/8). The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number is not recorded here any more: it moves whenever anything is added above it in that file, and it has moved twice for that reason without the arm itself changing. Read it off the report rather than from this note. The second describer beside it, added with the name member, has both arms reached and adds no partial point, and the id member's own refusals add none either: every arm of the set check, the length check and the two kind checks is reached by a test. The value types add no partial point either. Every arm of every reader is reached: each type has a test accepting its form and a test refusing the value the neighbouring type would accept, the duration walk is reached at each of its refusals including the years-and-months arm and the overflow, and both arms of the bound that cuts a quoted value are reached, by a value at the bound and by one whose cut would otherwise land inside a surrogate pair. The operator table adds no partial point either. Both arms of the acceptance walk are reached, by a pair the table accepts and by one it does not; both arms of the value-type refusal are reached, by an operator that takes a value and by one that takes none; and the two arms that throw rather than answer, an operator with no row and a refusal asked for a pair the table accepts, are each reached by a test. The composition stage adds no partial point either. Every refusal in the walk is reached by a document written to trip it, both directions of the group-count check are reached by an object carrying one member and by one carrying two, the depth arm is reached at the deepest allowed level and one past it, and the member walk is reached by a condition, by a nested group and by a member that is not an object. The field vocabulary adds no partial point either. Both arms of the row walk in the table are reached, by a field that has a row and by one that does not; both arms of the name lookup are reached, by a declared name and by a name differing from one only by case; and every arm of the stage that reads a condition's field is reached, by a condition naming a declared field, by one carrying no field member, by one whose field is not a string, by one naming a field the table does not declare and by a nested group holding each of those. The pointer resolver's arms are reached the same way: an empty pointer, a pointer with no leading slash, an absent member, an index past the end of an array, a token that is not a number, a descent into a value that is neither object nor array, and both escapes in the order the standard decodes them. The operator table's second type column adds no partial point either, and it is the one entry here where every arm is a copy of an arm already described: both directions of the field-type walk are reached, by an operator that applies to a field of the type asked about and by one that does not, and both arms of the field-type refusal are reached, by a pair the table refuses and by the accepted pair it throws for rather than answers. The stage that reads a condition's operator adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition with no operator member, one whose operator is a number rather than a string, one naming an operator no operator has, one naming an operator that does not apply to a field of that field's type, one naming an operator the field's own row does not declare, and one that is accepted. The two narrowed refusals beside it are reached the same way, including both arms of the guard that throws rather than building a refusal for a pair the field accepts. The stage that reads a condition's value adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition writing no value where the operator takes one, a condition writing no value where the operator takes a list, a value beside an operator that takes none, an operator that takes none and is written correctly, a list where one value belongs, one value where a list belongs, an empty list, a member of a list that does not parse beside members that do, and a value that does not parse where one belongs. The dispatch beside it is reached at each of its seven arms and at the throw a type with no reader takes, and the third column on the operator table is reached in both directions, by an operator written with a list and by one written with a value. The type a value is parsed against is reached on both of its answers, the field's own type and the operator's single one, and on both ways of asking for a pair that has no answer. The compile table and the stage that walks a rule's conditions onto a query add no partial point either. Both arms of the pair lookup are reached, by a pair the table compiles and by one over a field it compiles with an operator it does not; both arms of the property claim are reached, by a document narrowing two properties and by one narrowing a property another condition already wrote; both arms of every write that can decline are reached, by a value the property carries and by one it cannot, and the year check is reached at each of its two comparisons; and both arms of the guard on the write are reached, by a query and by a null one. The reporting arm in MembershipApplier adds no partial point either. Each of its three levels is asked whether it is enabled before the line is built, and both the level test and the outcome test above it are reached on both answers: a collection whose membership moved, one the run left exactly as it was, and one whose apply threw, each against a logger that reports every level enabled. The evaluation adds no partial point either, and the two arms that would have added one are the reason its own types are shaped the way they are. The shape dispatch is split off the entry point that reads an item, so a reading of a shape nothing produces can be handed to it and its last arm executed; the reading's constructor is internal exactly wide enough for that fixture. The walk over a composition group ends on the negation rather than on a throw, because a group kind with no arm cannot be written in a document at all and an arm for one could never be executed. Every other arm is reached by a pair a document can write: each of the eight comparisons over one string, the two over a list of them, the eight over a number, the three over an instant and the four over a length of time, each in both directions; the two operators about absence on both answers; a value the library does not hold on every shape that can be absent; a list the library holds as a null and one it holds as empty; an instant with no kind and one in local time; and the refusal each shape raises for an operator it has no comparison for, over five fields whose own rows do not declare that operator.
